Subject: Review: MSA security exhibit / audit scope questions

Hi Logan / Laura,

Thanks for sharing the MSA and security exhibit. Legal at Greystone has a few asks before we can sign:

- Can you clarify the scope of "audit rights"? Our counsel is asking for a narrower scope (SOC 2 report + remediation summary) and no source-code access or unlimited on-site inspections.
- Pen-test language: we need to agree windows and notice periods. We prefer 30-45 days notice for any external testing, and staging-only access (no production).
- Evidence cadence: our security team is used to a ticketed evidence model (monthly delivery of requested artifacts) rather than ad-hoc bulk uploads. Can Redwood support that?

I've attached a short summary of our legal questions (HealthEdge_MSA_questions_20260610.pdf).

Can we get a proposed redline and a suggested operational cadence (who on your side will be the evidence owner / contact)? If helpful, Chris (cc'd) is our security lead and can jump on a 30-min call.

Best,
Carmen

Laura / Ben / Monica — looping you in for legal + sec input. Carmen (external) is asking for a narrower audit right and explicit operational restrictions on pen tests and evidence delivery. I'll suggest a middle path to avoid long negotiation cycles:

1) Moderated inspection model ("inspection-lite"): contract language that limits Audit Rights to receipt of:
   - Latest SOC 2 Type II report (or SOC 2 bridge letter) and an executive summary of any open remediation items;
   - Limited access to artifacts via a ticketed evidence queue (monthly ticket turnarounds);
   - No source-code review and no unfettered on-site access except by written request and mutual agreement.

2) Pen test windows: offer 2 planned external penetration-test windows per year (customer-requestable), plus an option for an ad-hoc test for high-severity incidents. Notice: 14-45 day window depending on whether tests are internal vs. third-party external. All testing to occur in staging; ephemeral credentials only; scope to exclude customer data.

3) Operational owners: Monica as evidence owner and Ben as pen-test ops contact. Legal (Laura) to draft the redlines for the security exhibit and order form clause to reflect the limitations above.

Action: Laura — can you produce a redline we can share back to Carmen that limits the audit rights as described and includes the pen-test windows/notice language? Karthik — I will include the proposed language in the order form so sales has a clean playbook.

Thanks — I'll propose a 30-min call with Carmen + Chris for next week if legal needs to walk the language.

—Logan

Logan / Ben — thanks for the outline. I drafted a targeted set of redlines that aim to preserve Greystone's ability to validate controls while protecting Redwood's operational constraints. Key points in the attached redline (redline_MSA_security_exhibit_20260611.pdf):

- Audit scope: limited to (a) Redwood-provided SOC 2 Type II report (or succeeding attestation) and (b) an executive summary of remediation activities for exceptions identified in the report. No right to source code, system-level logs older than 90 days without a court order, or direct DB access.
- Inspection mechanics: evidence delivered via a ticketing queue (e.g., shared drive + a ticket) with a 30-calendar-day turnaround for non-sensitive artifacts; expedited 5-business-day SLA for high-priority requests tied to documented incidents.
- Pen testing: add specific language: 2 scheduled external tests per 12 months, customer must provide test scope and tool list at least 21 calendar days prior for third-party tests; Redwood may request postponement for operational stability but will not unreasonably withhold access; testing confined to non-production environments unless mutually agreed for a specific remediation exercise.
- Confidentiality & redaction: Redwood can redact IP-protective elements and vendor-facing details; we also define an intermediary review step where Redwood's security team vets requests for feasibility before release.

I've included a few alternate phrasings for the notice periods (21 days vs. 45 days) — recommend we offer 21 days as the default and allow 45 for very large scope tests.

Attached: redline_MSA_security_exhibit_20260611.pdf (contains the markup). Please review and I'll prepare a clean copy to share externally once you sign off.

Laura Bennett

Redwood Inference

Carmen / HealthEdge team — thanks for the questions and patience while we worked this through internally. Summary of what Redwood can commit to and next steps: 

1) Contract language: Redwood will provide a redlined security exhibit that:
   - Restricts audit rights to receipt of SOC 2 Type II reports (or successor attestations) and an executive remediation summary;
   - Preserves a ticketed evidence flow with a standard 30-calendar-day turnaround for routine artifact requests and a 5-business-day SLA for high-priority incident-related evidence;
   - Explicitly excludes source code and routine DB access; on-site inspections allowed only by separate written agreement.

2) Pen-test scheduling: proposed operational model:
   - Two planned external test windows per 12 months (customer-requested); default notice 21 calendar days for third-party external tests, 14 days for internal/security-team-led scans; option to request up to 45 days for larger scopes; testing confined to staging unless mutually agreed.

3) Operational owners & evidence flow: Monica Patel will be Greystone's primary evidence point-of-contact at Redwood (monica.patel@redwood.com). Ben Carter will coordinate pen-test logistics and staging access. We'll use a shared Drive folder for artifacts and a ticket (Drive + ticket) to track requests — link below.

4) Attachments & links: I've attached our proposed redline (HealthEdge_MSA_redlines_v1.docx) and included the drive + docusign links. Once you confirm the approach, we'll send the redline as a tracked PDF and schedule a 30-min sync next week (proposed times: Tue 16 Jun 10:00am PT or Wed 17 Jun 3:00pm PT).

If you want 1:1 time with Ben to discuss testing tools and safe-scoped test plans, we can set a separate technical call.

Next steps: Carmen — please confirm which time works and whether you want 21-day default notice or to request 45 for the initial agreement. We'll aim to keep this in an order-form appendix so it doesn't block standard MSA timelines.
